claims.text: The feedstock is AlCrFeNiSi powder with a particle-size distribution optimized for additive manufacturing.
Uniformly preheating the AlCrFeNiSi powder bed to 450–550°C will reduce thermal gradients.
Reduced thermal gradients will lower residual stresses in the miniature components.
The proposed preheating intervention will improve the mechanical properties of the miniature components.
A high-frequency induction coil can provide in-situ volumetric preheating of the powder bed.
Real-time closed-loop thermal feedback will ensure a uniform powder-bed temperature distribution.
The 450–550°C powder-bed preheating window is applicable to AlCrFeNiSi component geometries 0.5–2 mm thick.
Reduced thermal gradients and slower, controlled solidification will produce a uniform, fine-grained microstructure.
Preheating minimizes the temperature difference between the melt pool and surrounding powder.
Reducing the temperature difference between the melt pool and surrounding powder slows solidification.
Reducing the temperature difference between the melt pool and surrounding powder reduces thermal shock.
Uniform heating promotes homogeneous phase formation during deposition.
Uniform heating promotes stress relaxation during deposition.
Relative to conventional high-thermal-load builds, induction-preheated components will have significantly lower residual stresses.
Relative to conventional high-thermal-load builds, induction-preheated components will have enhanced ductility.
Relative to conventional high-thermal-load builds, induction-preheated components will have enhanced yield strength.
Relative to conventional high-thermal-load builds, induction-preheated components will require less post-processing.
Standard laser deposition without preheating produces high thermal gradients.
Standard laser deposition without preheating produces substantial residual stresses.
Standard laser deposition without preheating produces heterogeneous microstructures.
